Mechanical Senses","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":198,"printedEnd":210,"pdfStart":216,"pdfEnd":228,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"The mechanical senses include the vestibular sense, body sensation, pain, and itch. Different receptors and central pathways convey information about balance, touch, and bodily conditions."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Pain is not a simple measure of physical damage; neural and emotional factors influence it. Track where signals enter the spinal cord, how they are interpreted, and the different approaches discussed for relieving pain."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m6-2-study-1","text":"Balance, movement, and body position"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Mechanical senses respond to movement, pressure, stretch, and other forms of physical stimulation. The vestibular system in the inner ear helps detect head movement and orientation, supporting balance and coordination with vision. Proprioceptive and somatosensory pathways convey information about the body and the contact it makes with its environment. Different receptors and neural routes specialize for different kinds of stimulation rather than sending a single generic message called 'touch'."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m6-2-study-2","text":"How somatosensation reaches the brain"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Receptors in skin, muscles, joints, and other tissues initiate neural signals that travel through spinal and brain pathways. The central nervous system organizes these signals into representations of body regions and sensory qualities. Touch, temperature, position, itch, and pain are related but not interchangeable experiences. Their pathways can partly differ, so a change in one sensation does not necessarily mean every aspect of feeling is lost."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m6-2-study-3","text":"Pain: a warning system, not a simple gauge"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Nociceptive activity provides information about potentially harmful events, but experienced pain is shaped by neural processing and circumstances. The amount of tissue damage does not map perfectly onto reported pain. Spinal circuits, descending brain influences, attention, and emotion can amplify or reduce the response. Emotional distress can be painful without a new physical injury. This distinction helps explain why pain management may target more than one biological or psychological process."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m6-2-study-4","text":"Relief, itch, and practical contrasts"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Pain can be altered through several methods, including medications and processes that recruit the body's own pain-modulating systems. Different approaches have limitations and cannot all be expected to work for every condition. Itch is a distinct, often irritating sensation that can promote scratching and must not simply be treated as a mild form of pain. A strong revision answer differentiates the trigger, receptor, central pathway, and subjective experience for each mechanical sense."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m6-2-h01","text":"Vestibular Sensation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sensations from the vestibular organ detect the tilt of the head and the head’s acceleration.","sourcePrintedPage":198,"sourcePdfPage":216,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They cannot swim or float because they are often upside-down .","sourcePrintedPage":198,"sourcePdfPage":216,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When the head tilts, the otoliths push against hair cells and excite them, telling the brain the direction of tilt.","sourcePrintedPage":198,"sourcePdfPage":216,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The three semicircular canals , oriented in perpendicular planes, are filled with a fluid and lined with hair cells.","sourcePrintedPage":198,"sourcePdfPage":216,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Acceleration of the head at any angle causes the fluid in one of these canals to move, just as the water in a bucket will splash if you jerk the bucket from side to side.","sourcePrintedPage":198,"sourcePdfPage":216,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The fluid then pushes against the hair cells in the semicircular canals, setting up action potentials.","sourcePrintedPage":198,"sourcePdfPage":216,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Unlike the saccule and utricle, the semicircular canals record only the rate of acceleration, not the position of the head at rest.","sourcePrintedPage":198,"sourcePdfPage":216,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Whales are 10 million times as massive as mice, but their vestibular organ .","sourcePrintedPage":198,"sourcePdfPage":216,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m6-2-h02","text":"Somatosensation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The ions to enter and start an action potential .","sourcePrintedPage":199,"sourcePdfPage":217,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"On average, women can detect grooves systems for cooling and heating display an interesting asymmetry: Cold-sensitive neurons in the spinal cord exhibit little response to a constant low temperature, but they respond to a drop in .","sourcePrintedPage":200,"sourcePdfPage":218,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Szechuan peppers also stimulate the heat receptors, and in addition stimulate nerves.","sourcePrintedPage":201,"sourcePdfPage":219,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Each spinal nerve innervates (connects to) a limited area of the body .","sourcePrintedPage":202,"sourcePdfPage":220,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When the primary sensory cortex (S1) is inactive, either because of damage or cells nonfunctional until they regenerate over the next three to five months .","sourcePrintedPage":207,"sourcePdfPage":225,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Unfortunately, the results so far have been disappointing, because the drugs barrier.","sourcePrintedPage":207,"sourcePdfPage":225,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m6-2-h10","text":"Itch"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Or something identified special receptors for itch and a special peptide that itch releases in the nervous system .","sourcePrintedPage":207,"sourcePdfPage":225,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If an insect crawls slowly across your skin, that is one cause of itch.","sourcePrintedPage":207,"sourcePdfPage":225,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The two types of itch sensation travel in parallel paths to the brain.","sourcePrintedPage":207,"sourcePdfPage":225,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Itch receptors respond slowly, and when they do, their axons transmit impulses at only half a meter per second.","sourcePrintedPage":208,"sourcePdfPage":226,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Itch is useful because it directs you to scratch the itchy area and remove whatever is irritating your skin.","sourcePrintedPage":208,"sourcePdfPage":226,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Your brain is not satisfied until you scratch hard enough to produce mild pain, because pain inhibits itch .","sourcePrintedPage":208,"sourcePdfPage":226,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The inhibitory relationship between pain and itch is clear evidence that itch is not a type of pain.","sourcePrintedPage":208,"sourcePdfPage":226,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Further evidence is the demonstration that blocking itch fibers does not reduce pain .","sourcePrintedPage":208,"sourcePdfPage":226,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m6-2-h11","text":"In Closing: The Mechanical Senses"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"You have learned that pain messages go to both the brain’s touch area (somatosensory cortex) and its emotion area (amygdala and related structures).","sourcePrintedPage":208,"sourcePdfPage":226,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The body senses provide us with information, and they are also an important source of pleasure or displeasure.","sourcePrintedPage":208,"sourcePdfPage":226,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When a dentist gives you Novocain before drilling a tooth, part of your face becomes numb.","sourcePrintedPage":208,"sourcePdfPage":226,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"But when you try to scratch it, you feel nothing because the touch and pain sensations are still numb.","sourcePrintedPage":208,"sourcePdfPage":226,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Evidently, the effects of Novocain wear off faster for itch than for touch that responds to 44° C will respond the same way regardless of whether the skin was hotter, cooler, or the same temperature a minute or two Input from the pain/temperature pathway to the thalamus and then to the somatosensory cortex reports the intensity and location of the pain.","Imagine yourself in this experiment: You sit in front of a computer screen, playing a virtual ball-tossing game with two people your own age.","Experimenters monitored people’s brain activity during this virtual ball-throwing task and found increased activity in the cingulate cortex, an area responsive to the emotional aspects of pain.","Later studies found that this type of social exclusion does not always activate pain areas, but it often activates areas associated with evaluating others’ actions—that is, “why are they acting this way?”.","A study with more intense hurt feelings, based on remembering a recent romantic breakup, while looking at a photo of the ex-boyfriend or girlfriend, activated not only the cingulate cortex but also the sensory areas responsive to physical pain.","Researchers repeated the virtual ball-tossing study, but they gave some people acetaminophen and others a placebo.","Those taking acetaminophen exhibited less response in the cingulate cortex and other emotionally responsive areas. The researchers also asked college students to keep daily records about hurt feelings and social pain, while some took daily acetaminophen pills and others took a placebo.","However, there is a price to pay: People taking acetaminophen also","The brain puts the brakes on prolonged pain by opioid mechanisms — sys t ems that respond to opiate drugs and similar chemicals.","The discovery of opiate receptors was important because it revealed that opiates act on the nervous system rather than the injured tissue.","The brain produces several types of endorphins, which relieve different types of pain, such as the pain from a cut versus the pain from a burn.","However, morphine does block messages from thinner axons that convey slow, dull pain such as postsurgical pain. Anything that causes pain increases the breathing rate, and the opiates that decrease pain also decrease breathing, with potentially fatal consequences.","The input from gentle touch or top-down influences from the prefrontal cortex inhibits the pain messages in the spinal cord.","Despite much public enthusiasm for the pain-relieving potential of cannabinoids, high-quality research on this topic so far has been sparse.","Neuropathic pain is difficult to treat, and therefore any benefit from cannabinoids is encouraging. Wearing a skin patch with a high concentration of capsaicin for an hour produces a temporary burning sensation, but it causes an excessive buildup of calcium in the heat and pain neurons, and it damages those neurons’ mitochondria, rendering the cells nonfunctional until they regenerate over the next three to five months.","Unfortunately, the results so far have been disappointing, because the drugs they developed do not cross the blood-brain barrier.","Or something else altogether?” The answer is that itch is a separate sensation.","Researchers identified special receptors for itch and a special peptide that itch releases in the nervous system.","If an insect crawls slowly across your skin, that is one cause of itch.","The two types of itch sensation travel in parallel paths to the brain. Itch receptors respond slowly, and when they do, their axons transmit impulses at only half a meter per second.","Itch is useful because it directs you to scratch the itchy area and remove whatever is irritating your skin.","Your brain is not satisfied until you scratch hard enough to produce mild pain, because pain inhibits itch. The inhibitory relationship between pain and itch is clear evidence that itch is not a type of pain.","Further evidence is the demonstration that blocking itch fibers does not reduce pain.","You have learned that pain messages go to both the brain’s touch area (somatosensory cortex) and its emotion area (amygdala and related structures).","The body senses provide us with information, and they are also an important source of pleasure or displeasure.","When a dentist gives you Novocain before drilling a tooth, part of your face becomes numb.","But when you try to scratch it, you feel nothing because the touch and pain sensations are still numb. Evidently, the effects of Novocain wear off faster for itch than for touch and pain.","They’re also presented in alphabetical order with definitions in the book’s Subject Index/Glossary at the end of
